summary: This RFC defines an extra header field for Abuse Reporting Format reports so the source port of the connection involved in an abuse incident can be identified. It updates RFC 6591.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC adds a Source-Port field to Abuse Reporting Format reports. Together with Source-IP, the port helps identify the TCP connection from which the reported message originated.

subtitle: An ARF field for recording the TCP source port associated with an abuse report.

tldr.problem: When many clients share an IP address, a Source-IP value alone may not identify the origin of an abuse incident.
tldr.mechanism: The Source-Port field records the client port of the TCP connection corresponding to Source-IP.
tldr.outcome: The field adds connection detail to ARF reports and updates RFC 6591; accurate timing matters because ports may be reused quickly.

today: RFC 6692 is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 6591. The unit metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates RFC 6692.

sections.title: Why the Port Is Needed
sections.content:
Abuse Reporting Format reports describe email abuse incidents and may include the source IP address. When IP address sharing is used, that address alone may not uniquely identify the origin of abuse.

This RFC adds a field for the source port so the report can identify the connection more completely.
sections.plainLanguage: Several users may share an IP address. Adding the connection's source port provides another value to distinguish the origin.

sections.title: The Source-Port Field
sections.content:
The new ARF header field is named Source-Port. When present, it MUST contain the client port of the TCP connection from which the reported message originated, matching the connection described by Source-IP.

A report that includes Source-IP SHOULD also include Source-Port unless the port is unavailable. The field is RECOMMENDED for authentication-failure reports.
sections.plainLanguage: Source-Port records the client-side TCP port for the same connection as Source-IP. Reports should include it when the value is available.

sections.title: Time Accuracy, Registration, and Security
sections.content:
Source ports can be recycled quickly, so accurate clocks matter when matching a report to connection records. A generator that includes Arrival-Date MAY express the time in UTC.

IANA added Source-Port to the Feedback Report Header Fields registry. The RFC says the extension adds no new security considerations beyond those in the ARF specification.
sections.plainLanguage: Because a port can be reused, an accurate timestamp helps match it to the right connection. The new field is registered for feedback reports.
